'''James Taft''' "'''Jimmer'''" '''Fredette'''<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.namecandy.com/celebrity-baby-names/blog/2010/12/15/these-basketball-players-have-uncommon-skills-and-names |title=These Basketball Players Have Uncommon Skills and Names |publisher=NameCandy |date=December 15, 2010 |access-date=March 17, 2011 |archive-date=December 18, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101218121858/http://www.namecandy.com/celebrity-baby-names/blog/2010/12/15/these-basketball-players-have-uncommon-skills-and-names |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Eric |last=Medved |url=http://blog.timesunion.com/medved/jimmer-goes-a-long-way-in-repeating-his-amazing-2009-performance-against-zona/1392/ |title=Jimmer goes a long way in repeating his amazing 2009 performance against 'Zona |newspaper=Albany Times Union |date=December 12, 2010 |access-date=March 17, 2011 |archive-date=October 16, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121016075455/http://blog.timesunion.com/medved/jimmer-goes-a-long-way-in-repeating-his-amazing-2009-performance-against-zona/1392/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> (born February 25, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who serves as the managing director of the [[United States men's national 3x3 team|USA Basketball 3x3 Men's National Team]]. Fredette was the 2011 [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|National Player of the Year]] in [[college basketball]], after ranking as the leading scorer in all of [[NCAA Division I]] during his senior season for the [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU Cougars]]. He was subsequently selected with the 10th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]].

Fredette played for several professional teams in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] and [[NBA Development League]], as well as internationally. Fredette was the [[CBA Most Valuable Player]] in 2017, and he was a member of the [[Greek Basket League|GBL's]] championship team in 2020. Fredette began competing in [[3x3 basketball]] in 2022 and won two gold medals and one silver medal in international play. In 2024, Fredette represented [[United States at the Olympics|Team USA]] at the [[2024 Summer Olympics]] as a member of the first USA Basketball 3x3 Men's National Team to compete at the Olympics.

==Early life==
Fredette was born in [[Glens Falls, New York]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jimmer_Fredette/Summary/9263 |title=Jimmer Fredette |publisher=RealGM |access-date=March 3, 2011}}</ref> to parents Al and Kay Fredette, as the youngest of three children.<ref name=Layden>{{cite magazine |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/tim_layden/03/18/byu/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090322141143/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/tim_layden/03/18/byu/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 22, 2009 |title=With a crowd behind him, Fredette hoping to take BYU to new heights |first=Tim |last=Layden |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=March 18, 2009 |access-date=January 26, 2011}}</ref> His mother wanted to call him something unique and nicknamed him "Jimmer".

From his early childhood, Fredette showed unusual dedication to athletics. His older brother TJ recalled, "He was the most determined, competitive four-year-old I had ever seen." TJ helped him train for his basketball career since before kindergarten.<ref>{{cite web |last=King |first=Jason |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/news?slug=jn-byu031810 |title=Oh, brother, BYU survives |publisher=RRivals.com |access-date=March 17, 2011 |date=March 18, 2010}}</ref> He regularly played with TJ, seven years older, and TJ's friends on the family's backyard court. Fredette was able to hit [[three-point field goal|three-pointers]] at age 5, and developed moves to get around his larger opponents. TJ also remembered that his brother "willed himself to find ways to win, even if he was physically outmatched. From the time he was 10, I was telling everybody he was going to make the NBA."<ref name=Anderson2>{{cite magazine |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1181209/2/index.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110128060619/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1181209/2/index.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 28, 2011 |title=A Real Jimmer Dandy |first=Kelli |last=Anderson |magazine=Sports Illustrated |page=2 |date=January 31, 2011 |access-date=January 29, 2011}}</ref>

Other family members assisted Fredette in his development. His father, a financial adviser, introduced him to schoolyard competition against adults at age eight. As Fredette developed, his father took him on occasional road trips to [[Hartford, Connecticut|Hartford]] and New York City for more intense competition, and also helped to coach his AAU teams. His mother allowed him to bounce basketballs throughout the house, and even built a dribbling studio for him in their basement. Her brother Lee Taft, a personal trainer who now operates a speed training school in [[Indianapolis]], started him on running drills as a five-year-old, and still works with Fredette.<ref name=Anderson2/>

Fredette also has an older sister, Lindsay, [[Miss Teen USA 1998|Miss Teen New York 1998]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://issuu.com/thechronicle/docs/chronicle_jimmer |title=Section 2: Jimmer Fredette Chronicle |newspaper=The Chronicle |location=Glens Falls, New York |page=3 |date=December 2–8, 2010 |access-date=January 26, 2011}}</ref> Fredette's father became a member of [[the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] at the age of 18 after meeting [[Missionary (LDS Church)|missionary]] Kimball Rogers, who would end up being the father of Fredette's BYU teammate Stephen Rogers.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/700102377/BYU-basketball-reunites-Fredette-Rogers-families.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110123040016/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/700102377/BYU-basketball-reunites-Fredette-Rogers-families.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 23, 2011 |title=BYU basketball reunites Fredette, Rogers families |access-date=February 27, 2011 |author=Swensen, Jason |date=January 20, 2011 |publisher=Deseret News}}</ref> Fredette's mother is a Catholic. Fredette, along with his two older siblings, chose to become Latter-day Saints after their parents allowed them to choose their religion.<ref name=Layden/>{{dead link|date=June 2018}}

==High school career==
Fredette was ranked among the nation's top 75 shooting guards by ESPN.com in high school. He was Glens Falls High School's all-time leading scorer, ranking 16th on New York's all-time scoring list, with 2,404 points.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bronstein |first=Jonah |url=http://www.niagara-gazette.com/sports/byu-star-jimmer-fredette-comes-to-ub/article_05416a32-413b-51c5-8656-dce5fffa7ee3.html |title=BYU star Jimmer Fredette comes to UB |publisher=Niagara Gazette |date=December 29, 2010 |access-date=March 17, 2011}}</ref> Until February 24, 2015, Fredette held the all-time Section 2 high school record, when he was surpassed by Lake George senior Joel Wincowski.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://poststar.com/sports/basketball/high-school-and-prep/boys/joel-wincowski-passes-jimmer-sets-section-ii-record/article_eddf3c1a-bc98-11e4-83c8-077a263ec968.html |title=Joel Wincowski passes Jimmer, sets Section II record |work=PostStar.com |date=February 24, 2015 |access-date=February 24, 2015}}</ref> Fredette was named first-team all-state by the New York State Sportswriters Association and the ''[[Times Union (Albany)|Times Union]]'' as a junior and senior. He had several memorable on-court moments in his career at Glens Falls, including 12 different 40-point performances in his senior season,{{citation needed|date=April 2011}} and a shot against Voorheesville High School's Andrew Catellier in the season opener of his junior year in which he banked a three-pointer off the glass and in with his opposite hand to force overtime at the end of regulation.{{citation needed|date=April 2011}} In his senior season Fredette led his team to a 25–2 record and the Class A State Championship game which they lost, 58–48, to a [[Peekskill High School]] team led by future [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse University]] forward [[Mookie Jones]]. He played AAU for the Albany City Rocks alongside future [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State University]] point guard [[Talor Battle]] and Mark Domaracki.<ref>{{cite news |access-date=November 17, 2010 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/slideshow/2010/03/16/sports/ncaabasketball/20100316-NCAA_4.html |title=Defining the Great Midmajor Player |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=March 16, 2010}}</ref> Fredette averaged 25 points per game to help the Rocks to a third-place win over the Minnesota Magic at the 2006 AAU National Championships.<ref name="byucougars_profile">{{cite web |url=http://www.byucougars.com/Profile.jsp?ID=3062 |title=BYU Men's Basketball Athlete Profile (Jimmer Fredette) |publisher=BYUCougars.com |access-date=March 17, 2011 |archive-date=June 2, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110602115050/http://www.byucougars.com/Profile.jsp?ID=3062 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Despite his high school accolades, he went largely unnoticed by the traditional "basketball powers".<ref name="Anderson2"/> He received offers from 12 schools<ref name="Rec">{{cite web |url=http://www.heraldextra.com/sports/college/byu/basketball/article_9f04220e-b44d-51f2-936b-f3cdba071f8b.html |title=A look back: Jimmer finds way to BYU with a big assist from a Syracuse coach |author=Jason Franchuk |date=December 5, 2010 |work=[[Daily Herald (Utah)|The Daily Herald]] |access-date=February 26, 2011 |archive-date=February 9, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110209100644/http://www.heraldextra.com/sports/college/byu/basketball/article_9f04220e-b44d-51f2-936b-f3cdba071f8b.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> and ultimately chose to attend BYU,<ref name="Rec"/> which was his sister Lindsay's alma mater.

==College career==
Fredette played basketball collegiately at [[Brigham Young University]] (BYU) from 2007 to 2011. He wore jersey number 32 and majored in [[American studies]].

===Freshman year===
Fredette played in all 35 games for the [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU Cougars]] as a true freshman, helping BYU earn a 27–8 record and capture the [[Mountain West Conference]] regular season championship. He averaged 18.5 minutes, 7.0 points, 1.7 assists, 1.1 rebounds per game, and was the team's fifth-leading scorer.<ref name=byucougars_profile/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/6434/jimmer-fredette |title=Jimmer Fredette Stats, News, Photos |publisher=ESPN |access-date=March 17, 2011}}</ref>

===Sophomore year===
{{see also|2008–09 BYU Cougars men's basketball team}}
Fredette played in all 33 games of his sophomore season starting 32 of them. He was second on the team in scoring (16.2), three-point shooting percentage (.382), three-point makes (52), and free throw percentage (.847), and first in steals (1.5) and assists (4.1). He scored in double figures 29 times and had 20-plus points 8 times. Fredette led the team in scoring 10 times, assists 19 times, and was named first team all Mountain West.<ref name=byucougars_profile/> Fredette became BYU's first point guard to earn first-team all-conference honors since Marty Haws in 1990.

===Junior year===
{{see also|2009–10 BYU Cougars men's basketball team}}
On December 28, 2009, Jimmer Fredette scored 49 points against the Arizona Wildcats, setting a new BYU record and a new McKale Center record for points scored in a single game.<ref>{{cite web |last=Leung |first=Diamond |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/878/fredette-for-49 |title=Fredette for 49 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=March 17, 2011 |date=December 29, 2009}}</ref>

On March 11, 2010, Fredette scored 45 points, shooting 10-for-23 from the field, and making 23-of-24 free throws, in his team's 95–85 win over TCU. His scoring broke the cumulative Mountain West Conference tournament and single-game tournament records. His free throw shooting broke the MWC tournament record for free throws in a single game.<ref>{{cite web |last=Leung |first=Diamond |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/6069/jimmer-fredette-with-another-record-breaking-night |title=Another record-breaking night for Fredette |date=March 12, 2010 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=March 17, 2011}}</ref>

On March 18, 2010, Fredette helped secure BYU's first-round win in the NCAA tournament. He scored 37 points and hit two three-pointers in double-overtime to seal the Cougars' 99–92 win over 10th-seeded Florida, the first time they had reached the second round of the tournament in 17 years. In doing so, he tied a BYU record for most points scored in an NCAA tournament game ([[Danny Ainge]], 1981).<ref>{{cite web |access-date=November 17, 2010 |url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300770252 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100322235030/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300770252 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 22, 2010 |title=Fredette sinks key 3-pointers as No. 7 BYU knocks out No. 10 Florida in 2OT |publisher=ESPN |date=March 18, 2010}}</ref>

Fredette considered forgoing his senior year and entering the draft after his junior year, and he was expected to be picked 25th to 30th, but he decided to stay at BYU and play his senior year.

===Senior year===
{{see also|2010–11 BYU Cougars men's basketball team}}
[[File:Jimmer-byu-wyo-3-5-2011.jpg|upright|thumb|Fredette playing for BYU]]
Fredette was named co-captain of his team alongside [[Jackson Emery]] and Logan Magnusson.<ref name=byucougars>{{cite web |url=http://www.byucougars.com/Filing.jsp?ID=14410 |title=Captains Announced for 2010–11 |publisher=BYU Men's Basketball Press Release |date=September 24, 2010 |access-date=March 17, 2011 |archive-date=March 1, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110301192622/http://www.byucougars.com/Filing.jsp?ID=14410 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He was the top-ranked point guard in the nation according to [[Rivals.com]]<ref>{{cite web |access-date=February 2, 2011 |url=http://collegebasketball.rivals.com/viewcbse.asp |title=College Basketball Power Rankings |work=rivals.com |date=February 2, 2011}}</ref> and led the nation in points per game despite frequently being double- or triple-teamed, which allowed him to open up shots for his teammates.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ksl.com/?sid=14552641&nid=272 |title=BYU X's & O's: Double-Team |publisher=KSL.com |date=February 27, 2011 |access-date=March 17, 2011}}</ref>

Fredette scored a season-high 47 points in BYU's road victory over [[BYU–Utah rivalry|archrival]] [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]] on January 11, 2011, scoring 32 in the first half including a 40-foot buzzer-beater to end the first half. He finished with 16 of 28 shooting, along with four rebounds and six assists. He also scored 39 against [[2010–11 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team|UNLV]] on January 5, 2011, and 33 in a rematch against the same [[University of Arizona]] team he scored 49 against his junior season.

On December 8, 2010, he returned to his hometown of Glens Falls, in what was dubbed "The Hometown Classic", to play [[2010–11 Vermont Catamounts men's basketball team|Vermont]] in the [[Glens Falls Civic Center]], scoring 26 and attracting a crowd of 6,300, nearly half of Glens Falls' population of 14,354.

On January 26, 2011, in the Mountain West Conference's first battle of top-10 teams, which attracted a crowd of over 22,700 at [[BYU]]'s [[Marriott Center]], Fredette scored 43 points against previously undefeated [[2010–11 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]], ending the game in a 71–58 victory. It was his third game that season to score over 40 points. When BYU played on the road in San Diego, BYU dealt SDSU its only other loss that season, with an 80–67 victory in which Fredette had 25 points, 9 assists and 3 rebounds.

He became the Mountain West Conference's all-time leading scorer on February 5, 2011, with a 29-point performance versus UNLV in the Marriott Center.

On March 7, 2011, Fredette was named both the Mountain West Conference's player of the year and the CBSSports.com National Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/14788241/national-awards-jimmer-clear-choice-as-top-player |title=National awards: Jimmer clear choice as top player |publisher=CBSSports.com |date=March 8, 2011 |access-date=March 17, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141022000813/http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/14788241/national-awards-jimmer-clear-choice-as-top-player |archive-date=October 22, 2014}}</ref> He was among the final ten candidates for the Bob Cousy Award.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cousyaward.com/docs/CousyAward2011.pdf |title=BASKETBALL HALL OF FAME ANNOUNCES FINAL TEN CANDIDATES FOR 2011 BOB COUSY AWARD |work=[[Bob Cousy Award]] |date=February 7, 2011 |access-date=July 7, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111002104704/http://www.cousyaward.com/docs/CousyAward2011.pdf |archive-date=October 2, 2011}}</ref>

On March 11, 2011, Fredette broke BYU's career scoring record, previously held by [[Danny Ainge]], in the semifinals of the Mountain West Conference Championship Tournament. He set the school's single-game scoring record with a career-high 52-point game against [[2010–11 New Mexico Lobos men's basketball team|New Mexico]], to whom BYU had lost twice in the regular season. He also set BYU's record for most points in one half by scoring 33 points in the first half of the game.<ref>{{cite news |last=Drew |first=Jay |url=http://www.sltrib.com/sltrib/cougars/51416210-88/points-byu-cougars-fredette.html.csp |title=Jimmer Fredette's 52 points carry BYU past New Mexico |publisher=The Salt Lake Tribune |date=March 11, 2011 |access-date=March 17, 2011}}</ref> Fredette and number 12-ranked BYU were unable to hold off an aggressive 5th-ranked San Diego State team in the Mountain West Conference championship game, and lost, 72–54.

On March 17, 2011, Fredette led 3rd-seeded BYU's scoring in the first round of the NCAA tournament with 32 points, leading the Cougars to a 74–66 victory over 14th-seeded Wofford, and for the second consecutive year BYU advanced to the second round of the NCAA tournament.<ref>{{cite news |last=Griffin |first=Andrew |url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/705368922/BYU-basketball-Jimmer-Fredette-turned-it-on-when-BYU-needed-it-most.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110319095453/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/705368922/BYU-basketball-Jimmer-Fredette-turned-it-on-when-BYU-needed-it-most.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 19, 2011 |title=Jimmer Fredette turned it on when BYU needed it most |work=Deseret News |date=March 17, 2011 |access-date=March 19, 2011}}</ref>

On March 19, 2011, Fredette again led BYU's scoring with 34 points as they defeated 11th-seeded Gonzaga, 89–67, and advanced to the third round of the NCAA Tournament ([[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Sweet Sixteen]]) for the first time since 1981, falling to the Florida Gators (in overtime) in a rematch of the game from the previous year.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310780252 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120718192137/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310780252 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 18, 2012 |title=Jimmer Fredette's 34 puts BYU in school's first Sweet 16 since 1981, but Fredette and BYU would fall short as they lost to the Florida Gators in over time 83–74 (Fredette had 32 points in his last game with BYU). |publisher=ESPN |date=March 19, 2011 |access-date=March 20, 2011}}</ref>

He was picked to the First-Team All-America by [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Jeff |last=Goodman |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |title=Goodman's 2010–11 All-America teams |work=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]] |publisher=Fox Sports Interactive Media |date=March 7, 2011 |access-date=June 21, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201123808/http://msn.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/duke-blue-devils-notre-dame-fighting-irish-represented-postseason-honors-030711 |archive-date=February 1, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/6434/jimmer-fredette |title=Jimmer Fredette Stats, News, Photos – Brigham Young Cougars – ESPN |publisher=ESPN |date=March 20, 2011 |access-date=March 20, 2011}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2019)===
On March 22, 2019, Fredette signed a two-year contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Suns Sign Jimmer Fredette |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-jimmer-fredette |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 27, 2019 |date=March 22, 2019}}</ref> He made his official return to the NBA a day later against his first NBA team, the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hield sets franchise season record for 3s, Kings beat Suns |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071767 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 27, 2019 |date=March 23, 2019}}</ref> In his next game on March 25, Fredette was given a standing ovation in his return to Utah in a loss against the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Suns vs. Jazz – Game Recap – March 25, 2019 – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071778 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 27, 2019 |date=March 25, 2019 |quote=Still, some of the loudest cheers of the night were for a Suns player: Jimmer Fredette, the Naismith Award winner at nearby BYU, went 1-for-10 for six points in 14 minutes in his second game back in the NBA after completing his season in China, saying afterward he was pretty amped-up.}}</ref> However, after only playing in six games and averaging only 3.7 points per game, on June 24, Phoenix declined to pick up the second-year option of Fredette's deal<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://arizonasports.com/nba/phoenix-suns/jimmer-fredette-join-warriors-summer-league-suns-decline-option|title=Jimmer Fredette to join Warriors after Suns decline option|first=Kevin|last=Zimmerman|website=Arizonasports.com|date=June 24, 2019|access-date=July 21, 2026}}</ref> and his short return to the NBA ended. ===Panathinaikos (2019–2020)===
On July 15, 2019, Fredette signed a two-year contract with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of Greece's [[Greek basketball league system|top-tier]] level [[Greek Basketball League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9shqjgalo8emwdkv/panathinaikos-lands-china-scoring-champ-fredette |title=Panathinaikos lands China scoring champ Fredette |website=EuroLeague.net |date=July 15, 2019 |access-date=July 15, 2019}}</ref>  When the Greek League suspended play due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Panathinaikos was named league champion.

Panathinaikos experienced serious financial difficulties as a result of the pandemic, and on July 4, 2020, the team announced that Fredette's contract was too heavy for the team's budget. As a result, Fredette was essentially laid off.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Askounis |first1=Johnny |title=Panathinaikos president: "Fredette is free to go" |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1077349/jimmer-fredette-still-looking-for-a-new-team/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=December 5, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116221752/https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1077312/panathinaikos-targeting-sam-dekker/ |archive-date=November 16, 2020 |language=en |date=July 4, 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Return to Shanghai (2020–2021)===
On September 6, Fredette confirmed via Twitter that he intended to return to the [[Shanghai Sharks]], and he made his return debut on October 18.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McDonald |first1=Ryan |title=Jimmer Fredette announces he's returning to the Shanghai Sharks |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2020/9/6/21425671/jimmer-fredette-shanghai-sharks-byu-basketball |website=[[Deseret News]] |access-date=December 5, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200907035131/https://www.deseret.com/sports/2020/9/6/21425671/jimmer-fredette-shanghai-sharks-byu-basketball |archive-date=September 7, 2020 |language=en |date=September 6, 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref> On October 20, he scored 26 points to lead all scorers as the Sharks earned their first win of the season, 95–88 over the Shanxi Sturgeons.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Harper |first1=Mitch |title=Jimmer Fredette Leads All Scorers In Shanghai Sharks First Win Of Season |url=https://kslsports.com/444307/jimmer-fredette-shanghai-sharks-leads-all-scorers/ |website=KSL Sports |publisher=[[KSL.com]] |access-date=December 5, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101135218/https://kslsports.com/444307/jimmer-fredette-shanghai-sharks-leads-all-scorers/ |archive-date=November 1, 2020 |date=October 21, 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref> Fredette became the Shanghai Sharks all time 3-point leader on December 29, 2020.

As a result of the pandemic, Fredette was forced to leave China early in 2021 and suspend his involvement with the Shanghai Sharks.  On August 5, 2021, as it became clear that foreign players likely would not be able to compete in the 2021–22 CBA season, Fredette was signed to the [[Denver Nuggets]] Summer League roster for the second time.<ref name="deseret.com"/> However, he almost immediately withdrew from Summer League play due to unspecified issues.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.deseret.com/2021/8/6/22613276/scratch-that-jimmer-fredette-reportedly-wont-play-in-nba-summer-league-after-all |title=Jimmer Fredette reportedly won't play in NBA Summer League after all |work=Deseret News |date=August 6, 2021 |access-date=January 30, 2022}}</ref>

===The Basketball Tournament===
Fredette has participated in [[The Basketball Tournament]] (TBT), a million-dollar winner-take-all summer tournament broadcast on the [[ESPN]] family of channels. In [[The Basketball Tournament 2017|TBT 2017]], he acted as coach for Team Fredette,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thetournament.com/news/who-are-team-fredette-tbt-2017 |title=Who Are: Team Fredette TBT 2017 |website=thetournament.com |date=2017 |access-date=August 3, 2018 |archive-date=December 4, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191204155448/https://www.thetournament.com/news/who-are-team-fredette-tbt-2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref> which lost in the first round to Team Utah, 100–97. In [[The Basketball Tournament 2018|TBT 2018]], he played for Team Fredette,<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2018/06/05/tbt-bracket-field-teams-jimmer-fredette-matt-barnes-overseas-elite |title=Jimmer Fredette, Matt Barnes Headline Deep Fields For Fifth Annual TBT |first=Tim |last=Hackett |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=June 5, 2018 |access-date=July 30, 2018}}</ref> leading the team to four wins and a spot in the semifinals, where they lost to [[Eberlein Drive]], 80–76.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thetournament.com/news/eberlein-drive-continues-magical-run-thrilling-semifinal-win-over-team-fredette |title=Eberlein Drive Continues Magical Run with Thrilling Semifinal Win Over Team Fredette |website=thetournament.com |date=August 2, 2018 |access-date=August 3, 2018 |archive-date=June 30, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190630151422/https://www.thetournament.com/news/eberlein-drive-continues-magical-run-thrilling-semifinal-win-over-team-fredette |url-status=dead}}</ref> He returned as a player in [[The Basketball Tournament 2022|TBT 2022]], with The Money Team.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.deseret.com/2022/6/22/23179049/jimmer-fredette-is-taking-his-shot-at-a-1-million-prize-in-the-basketball-tournament-byu-basketball |title=Jimmer Fredette is taking his shot at a $1 million prize in The Basketball Tournament |first=Brandon |last=Judd |website=[[Deseret News]] |date=June 22, 2022 |access-date=July 24, 2022}}</ref>

===3x3 basketball and Olympics===
In 2022, Fredette made his 3x3 debut at the 2022 Red Bull USA Basketball 3X East Regional, which took place October 8–9 in New York, and helped team NYC Blue win the event. On October 25, 2022, Fredette, [[Canyon Barry]], [[Kareem Maddox]], and Dylan Travis were named to the USA Men's 2022 3x3 AmeriCup team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 25, 2022 |title=USA Basketball Announces 2022 3x3 AmeriCup Rosters |url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2022/10/3x3-americup-rosters.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221026150943/https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2022/10/3x3-americup-rosters.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 26, 2022 |access-date=November 18, 2022 |website=www.usab.com |language=en-US}}</ref> At the 2022 FIBA 3x3 AmeriCup, which took place November 4–6 in Miami, Fredette and his team won gold.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 7, 2022 |title=USA's men and Canada's women win FIBA 3x3 AmeriCup 2022 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/3x3americup/2022/news/usa-s-men-and-canada-s-women-win-fiba-3x3-americup-2022 |access-date=November 18, 2022 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref> In FIBA 3x3 World Cup 2023, Fredette played for USA, winning the silver medal,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Overview {{!}} FIBA 3x3 World Cup 2023 |url=https://fiba3x3.com/2023/worldcup |access-date=June 6, 2023 |website=fiba3x3.com}}</ref> and Fredette was selected for the Team of the Tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 4, 2023 |title=MVP Stojacic headlines headlines men's Team of the Tournament at FIBA 3x3 World Cup 2023 |url=https://fiba3x3.com/2023/news/mvp-stojacic-headlines-headlines-men-s-team-of-the-tournament-at-fiba-3x3-world-cup-2023 |access-date=June 6, 2023 |website=fiba3x3.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2024, Fredette represented [[United States at the Olympics|Team USA]] at the [[2024 Summer Olympics]] as a member of the first [[USA Basketball]] 3x3 Men's National Team to compete at the Olympics.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Merrell |first1=Chloe |title=Jimmer Fredette headlines USA men's 3x3 basketball team for Paris 2024 |url=https://olympics.com/en/news/usa-basketball-3x3-mens-team-jimmer-fredette-paris-2024 |publisher=Olympics.com |access-date=July 5, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/jimmer-fredette_1954772 |title=FREDETTE Jimmer |work=[[Paris 2024 Olympics]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240730140313/https://www.olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/jimmer-fredette_1954772 |archive-date=July 30, 2024}} ([https://paris2024.rtve.es/es/paris-2024/atleta/jimmer-fredette_1954772 alternate link])</ref> Fredette suffered an adductor tear in the second pool play game and didn't play in four of the games, and the team was eliminated after going 2–5.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dallas |first1=Kelsey |title=Jimmer Fredette and the U.S. men's 3x3 basketball team are done at the Olympics |date=August 4, 2024 |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/08/04/jimmer-fredette-us-3x3-mens-basketball-eliminated-olympics/ |publisher=Deseret News |access-date=4 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Polacek |first1=Scott |title=USA Out of Olympic 3x3 Basketball Bracket amid Jimmer Fredette Injury, 2-5 Record |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10130748-usa-out-of-olympic-3x3-basketball-bracket-amid-jimmer-fredette-injury-2-5-record |publisher=Bleacher Report |access-date=4 August 2024}}</ref>

On April 23, 2025, Fredette announced his retirement from basketball.<ref>{{cite web|last=Grausz|first=Dylan|title=Basketball Star Jimmer Fredette Announces Retirement|url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/basketball_star_jimmer_fredette_announces_retirement/s1_17396_42094563|website=yardbarker.com|date=April 23, 2025|access-date=April 23, 2025}}</ref>

==Playing style and personality==
In a January 2011 article, ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' writer Kelli Anderson said about Fredette's playing style:

{{blockquote|Facing the opposition's best defender (or, more often, defenders), he pulls up going right or going left. He shoots off the dribble, off the wrong foot, off balance, off the glass. He finishes in traffic with a dozen deft moves, including a scoop shot, originating from his waist, that he can make with either hand.<ref name=Anderson1>{{cite magazine |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1181209/index.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110128165751/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1181209/index.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 28, 2011 |title=A Real Jimmer Dandy |first=Kelli |last=Anderson |magazine=Sports Illustrated |page=1 |date=January 31, 2011 |access-date=January 29, 2011}}</ref>}}

His skills were noted by several collegiate and NBA players across the country. [[Kevin Durant]] of the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] posted on his Twitter account that "Jimmer Fredette is the best scorer in the world!",<ref>{{cite web |url=http://blog.newsok.com/thunderrumblings/2011/01/28/kevin-durant-marvels-at-jimmer-fredette/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120709144218/http://blog.newsok.com/thunderrumblings/2011/01/28/kevin-durant-marvels-at-jimmer-fredette/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 9, 2012 |title=Kevin Durant marvels at Jimmer Fredette |publisher=Thunder Rumblings |date=January 28, 2011 |access-date=March 17, 2011}}</ref> while [[Steve Nash]] of the [[Phoenix Suns]] tweeted "Jimmer Fredette? That name's straight out of Hoosiers. No wonder he never misses."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.twitter.com/SteveNash/status/31075282408443904 |title=Steve Nash: Jimmer Fredette? |publisher=Twitter |date=January 28, 2011 |access-date=March 17, 2011}}</ref> [[Jared Sullinger]], a forward at [[Ohio State University]], said "Jimmer is going off right now. Pure scorer."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.twitter.com/Jared_Sully0/status/30480863779102720 |title=Jared Sullinger: Jimmer is going off now |publisher=Twitter |date=January 26, 2011 |access-date=March 17, 2011}}</ref>

Other facets of his personality were noted by other college coaches. Former [[Utah Utes]] coach [[Jim Boylen]] cited "swagger and confidence" as Fredette's biggest weapons, and [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova's]] [[Jay Wright (coach)|Jay Wright]] also remarked favorably on Fredette's on-court aggressiveness, comparing him to [[Pete Maravich]] in that respect. However, Kelli Anderson described Fredette as "fiercely competitive while remaining unassuming and likable," noting that [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] coach [[Sean Miller]] hugged Fredette after he scored 49 on the Wildcats.<ref name="Anderson1"/>

Fredette describes his older brother TJ as his biggest fan and supporter. TJ, a rapper whose song "Amazing" was written for his brother, said, "I see him play, and it gives me chills sometimes when he hits some of those big shots and the crowd is going crazy."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ksl.com/?nid=148&sid=14151663 |title=TJ Fredette talks about growing up with Jimmer |date=January 26, 2011 |first=Keith |last=McCord |publisher=[[KSL-TV|KSL]] |access-date=January 26, 2011}}</ref>

In an article published in ''Sports Illustrated'', [[Marcus Morris (basketball)|Marcus Morris]], a forward at Kansas, noted the work ethic and moral character Fredette exhibited while at USA Basketball camp. He said, "He's got heart. You can see he has a feel for the game, and he can shoot it from anywhere. Even if you try to box-and-one the guy, he brings it up and just pulls up from the hashmark. That's tough to guard."<ref name="TourneySI">{{cite web |url=http://tourney.si.com/2011/03/16/cover-kids-marcus-morris-talks-jimmer/ |title=Cover Kids: Marcus Morris Talks Jimmer |work=SI.com |date=March 16, 2011 |access-date=June 9, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110321010633/http://tourney.si.com/2011/03/16/cover-kids-marcus-morris-talks-jimmer/ |archive-date=March 21, 2011}}</ref>

An unusual set of Fredette fans resided in the [[Mount McGregor Correctional Facility]], a medium-security prison, where he and his older brother played games with the inmates. Fredette credits these experiences as helping with his focus in rough situations. The prison closed in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |first=Heather |last=Chaet |url=http://thestir.cafemom.com/sports/117593/ncaa_star_jimmer_fredette_went |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110321223806/http://thestir.cafemom.com/sports/117593/ncaa_star_jimmer_fredette_went |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 21, 2011 |title=NCAA Star Jimmer Fredette Went to Prison to Learn to Play Basketball |work=CafeMom.com |date=March 16, 2011 |access-date=June 9, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Jeff |last=Eisenberg |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/blog/the_dagger/post/Jimmermania-has-even-reached-the-New-York-prison?urn=ncaab-wp427 |title=Jimmermania has even reached the New York prison system |work=Rivals.Yahoo.com |date=April 5, 2011 |access-date=June 9, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://m.timesunion.com/local/article/Prison-set-to-close-but-not-quietly-5648057.php |title=Prison set to close, but not quietly |work=Times Union |access-date=February 4, 2018 |archive-date=December 4, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191204155553/https://m.timesunion.com/local/article/Prison-set-to-close-but-not-quietly-5648057.php |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Upon entering the NBA, Fredette struggled to find his game, with Yahoo Sports' Michael Lee noting that Fredette's inability to adjust from being a scorer to more of a role player could ultimately usher an end to his career.<ref>{{cite web |first=Michael |last=Lee |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/why-jimmer-fredette-has-been-such-a-big-bust-in-the-nba-023311779.html |title=Why Jimmer Fredette has been such a big bust in the NBA |work=Yahoo.com |date=October 21, 2015 |access-date=October 21, 2015}}</ref>

After signing with the CBA's [[Shanghai Sharks]], Fredette became a dominant player in the Chinese Basketball League, leading his team to the playoffs in 3 of his 4 years there. He also acquired the fan nickname "Jimo Dashen", which translates to "The Lonely Master" or "The Lonely God" in Chinese. Fredette commented on this during an interview: "It's not necessarily the same sense that you think about being lonely. In America, you just think you are by yourself and depressed and that type of stuff. But in this way, it more means that you're on top, and nobody is around you."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/2017/04/03/lonely-master-espn-features-former-byu-star-jimmer-fredette-new-documentary/100001190/ |title='The Lonely Master': ESPN features former BYU star Jimmer Fredette in new documentary |website=[[USA Today]] |access-date=November 17, 2017}}</ref>

Fredette became a leader on his team, although, particularly early in his CBA career, his primary form of communication with his teammates was via an interpreter.<ref>{{cite web |author=Les Carpenter |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/the-second-act-of-jimmer-mania-183331176.html |title=The second act of Jimmer Mania |publisher=Sports.Yahoo.com |date=January 30, 2017 |access-date=May 3, 2017}}</ref>
